findings.why: The Day 1 / Week 4 / Week 8 frames, matched to the 4- and 8-week stats, form a before/after progression, and AI-generated frames are not representative, unretouched evidence (the "not real results" note sits only in the footnote). The 8-week frame is the "dark spots faded" end state, and the headline repeats the timeline.
findings.fix: Relabel the frames as routine stages (e.g. "Week 8 · in the routine") with the AI-illustration note on the image itself, or replace them with real, unretouched study photos and their qualifier.

rule_hit_review.why: Matches F19 ("felt healthier after 4 weeks of usage") and is perception-worded; the creative should still name the study type with the window.
Matches F18 ("said their dark spots faded after 8 weeks"); acceptable if the study file confirms the 8-week duration.
Keeps "said ... felt" (F19), but "healthier" is vague and no study type or n is shown.
F18 verbatim and perception-worded; it must stay as "subjects said" and never be restated as "fades dark spots", and it needs the study-type and n qualifier.

tone_read: Calm and spec-led with no fear hook or hype, and the footnote is candid about the AI frames. The three-frame timeline is category-style transformation creative rather than Minimalist's education-first approach.
language_read: "10% Vitamin C" and "Vitamin C 10% Face Serum" are in house format, and the stats keep "subjects said" perception wording. "Dark spots faded" and "healthier" are outcome words that rely entirely on that perception framing.
